title: Quantum spin Hall crystals at fractional filling of twisted MoTe$_2$
authors: Xiaoyang Shen, Raul Perea-Causin, Christopher Ekman, Jiong-Hao Wang, Hui Liu, Emil J. Bergholtz
abstract: We predict and classify interaction-driven quantum spin Hall crystals (QSHCs), a class of states emerging at fractional filling through an interplay of topology and spontaneous translation-symmetry breaking. QSHCs form nearly degenerate manifolds whose members can realize distinct topological phases protected by time-reversal or valley $U(1)_v$ symmetry, with time-reversal acting nontrivially within the manifold. As a representative of this broad class of states we provide evidence for 9-fold quasi-degenerate $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ charge ordered QSHCs at $ν= -8/3$ of twisted bilayer MoTe$_2$ near a $5^\circ$ twist. Here a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ index organizes states related by lattice translation into three time-reversal invariant states with nontrivial $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topology and three time-reversal related doublets whose individual members spontaneously break time-reversal and carry a $U(1)_v$ protected spin-Chern number. Finally, we determine the conditions that favor QSHCs over closely competing intervalley-coherent crystals.
summary: This theoretical work predicts and classifies Quantum Spin Hall Crystals (QSHCs) in twisted bilayer $	ext{MoTe}_2$ at fractional filling. Using advanced mean-field calculations, the authors demonstrate a $\sqrt{3} 	imes \sqrt{3}$ QSHC state protected by specific symmetries. The research provides a detailed understanding of how intervalley interactions stabilize these topologically rich, charge-ordered phases.
main_problem: The paper aims to predict and classify interaction-driven Quantum Spin Hall Crystals (QSHCs) that emerge at fractional filling due to the interplay between topology and spontaneous translation-symmetry breaking.
main_result:
The system exhibits a $\sqrt{3} 	imes \sqrt{3}$ QSHC state at $
u = -8/3$ in twisted bilayer $	ext{MoTe}_2$, which forms a complex ground state manifold organized by a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ index.
method: The study employs Self-Consistent Hartree-Fock (SCHF) calculations performed in the crystal Brillouin zone, supplemented by topological characterization using Wilson loops and Chern numbers.
model_or_system: The physical system is twisted bilayer $	ext{MoTe}_2$. The analysis uses continuum models and mean-field approximations to study the interplay between topology, interaction effects, and lattice ordering.
key_observables: Spin-Chern number ($C_s$), valley Chern numbers ($C_K, C_{K'}$), crystal order parameters ($\Phi_\mu(\mathbf{Q})$), and energy splitting ($\Delta E$).
important_parameters:
Fractional filling ($
u = -8/3$), twist angle ($	heta \approx 5^\circ$), and interaction strength ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The primary approximation is the use of the Hartree-Fock mean-field theory, which is noted to be limited in capturing fully fractionalized topological orders.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the $\sqrt{3} 	imes \sqrt{3}$ QSHC structure, band structures for different phases (QSHC, AFMz, IVC), and phase diagrams showing the competition between these phases as a function of twist angle and interaction strength.
paper_structure: The paper systematically predicts QSHCs, analyzes the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ organization of the ground state manifold based on relative valley alignment ($\delta$), and quantitatively determines the energetic preference between different topological sectors using first-order energy corrections.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of symmetry protection ($\mathbb{Z}_2$ vs $U(1)_v$) and the quantitative determination of energy splittings in topological phases are highly relevant to understanding emergent order in strongly correlated electronic systems.
